eval_rule: validation and (report-only) test every max(500, steps/40) steps; selection only by validation
title: DBP-X with trainable FIR: least-squares start, pruning during training to 31 / 15 / 7 versus direct initialization at the target length
question: How much BER reduction does DBP-X keep at step FIR lengths 31, 15, 7 when (a) started at 255 by the full-band LS fit and pruned progressively during training, (b) started directly at the target length by the same LS fit (= truncation at 1 sps), (c) started at the target length by the joint LS fit of the cascade (L_D, L-BFGS), (d) cut abruptly from the trained 255? RM in both conventions with 4 and 3 RM per complex product. Ns = 20 (one span per step, as Lin 2021) is the reference.
model: dbpx.DBPX with a tap mask (e054_prune.Masked): D_total exact and fixed, Ns steps [symmetric FIR(255) circular FFT, Kerr phase R = 7], complex gain; start = physical taps + alpha of the E050 start choice (validation)

schedule.progressive: active half-length shrinks linearly from the previous to the new length over 'shrink' iterations, then 'fine' iterations
schedule.abrupt: control: cut at once, then shrink + fine iterations (same budget)
schedule.selection: per length: checkpoint with the minimum validation MSE during its fine part; test reported there

rm.columns: rm_direct_4, rm_direct_3 (direct symmetric FIR), rm_fft_4, rm_fft_3 (Xiao C_conv, scaled by 3/4 for 3 RM); 3 RM per complex product: Civelli 2025 (из литературы); all four are reported, the choice is pending (advisor)
rm.filters: sum of filter lengths Ns L and cascade support Ns (L - 1) + 1 against the accumulated dispersion memory 4 pi |c_total| = 270 symbols

rule_draft.report: per (Ns, length): mean, std, SE, range over seeds; share of the L = 255 level kept; RM in both conventions
rule_draft.limits: one schedule (no tuning of the schedule); circular files; one channel, one polarization, 1 sps
rule_draft.progressive_vs_others: progressive better than direct / direct_ld / abrupt at a length if the difference > 2 SE and > 2 std (reverse also reported)

value_filter.changes_next_step: yes: decides whether DBP-X can be cheap in the direct-convolution convention
value_filter.answered_in_literature: learned short filters in DBP are standard (Xiao 2025 uses filters of the step memory); not on our 1 sps data
value_filter.cheaper_without_training: no (E050 unit test: truncation without training fails)

ls_note: checked numerically: at 1 sps the uniform full-band LS fit of an L-tap FIR to exp(i c nu^2) equals the truncated inverse DTFT (relative difference <= 1.4e-6, grid limited) for L = 7 ... 255, Ns = 20, 40; the advice against truncation (Hager, Pfister 2020, footnote 1, из литературы) concerns oversampled signals with an out-of-band region, which does not exist here

arms.progressive: LS(=truncation) at 255, warm 3000, then per length 1000 shrink + 2000 fine
arms.direct: LS(=truncation) at the target length, trained for the same number of iterations the progressive arm spent to reach it
arms.direct_ld: joint cascade LS (Xiao L_D, L-BFGS 300 from the truncation, lowest L_D kept) at the target length, same budget
arms.abrupt: cut from the trained 255 at once, then 3000 per length
